q: In railway track terminology, the abbreviation 'LWR' stands for:
e: LWR stands for Long Welded Rail, a length of rail formed by welding several standard rails together so that expansion is restrained and a smoother, stronger track is obtained.

q: In the Railway Board's official circular series, the abbreviation 'RBE' stands for:
e: RBE stands for Railway Board Establishment, the series used for Railway Board circulars and orders dealing with establishment matters such as pay, allowances and service conditions.

q: In the delegation of financial powers on Indian Railways, the document 'SOP' stands for:
e: In the delegation of financial powers on Indian Railways, SOP stands for Schedule of Powers, the document that lays down the monetary limits up to which each authority may sanction expenditure.

q: In Government and railway accounts, the officer denoted by 'DDO' stands for:
e: DDO stands for Drawing and Disbursing Officer, the officer authorised to draw money from the treasury or bank and make payments on behalf of the Government.

q: In railway accident relief arrangements, the abbreviation 'ARME' stands for:
e: ARME stands for Accident Relief Medical Equipment, the specially equipped medical relief vans and scale-I equipment rushed to accident sites for first aid and rescue of injured passengers.

q: In railway official correspondence, the monthly report denoted by 'MCDO' stands for:
e: MCDO stands for Monthly Confidential Demi-Official, the confidential monthly demi-official report through which officers apprise higher authorities of important developments and performance.

q: In Indian Railways, the rule book denoted by 'G&SR' stands for:
e: G and SR stands for General and Subsidiary Rules, the basic rule book governing the working of trains and the duties of railway staff in train operations.

q: In railway signalling, the system 'IBS', provided to increase line capacity between two stations, stands for:
e: IBS stands for Intermediate Block Signalling, a system in which an intermediate block post splits a long block section into two parts, allowing more trains to run and increasing line capacity.

q: In railway track terminology, the abbreviation 'CWR' stands for:
e: CWR stands for Continuous Welded Rail, rail welded into very long lengths across many spans so that joints are virtually eliminated, giving a smoother ride and lower maintenance.

q: 'Rudrastra', the longest freight train of Indian Railways whose trial run was conducted in August 2025 between Ganjkhwaja and Garhwa Road, had a total length of about:
e: Rudrastra, formed by coupling six freight rakes with 345 wagons and seven locomotives, was about 4.5 km long, making it the longest freight train tried in Asia during its August 2025 trial between Ganjkhwaja and Garhwa Road.

q: India's first removable solar panel system between railway tracks, commissioned as a pilot project at Banaras Locomotive Works, Varanasi in August 2025, has an installed capacity of:
e: The pilot removable solar panel system installed between the tracks on Line No. 19 at Banaras Locomotive Works, Varanasi, uses 28 panels over a 70-metre stretch with a total installed capacity of 15 kWp.

q: India's first hyperloop test track, completed in December 2024 at IIT Madras with the support of Indian Railways, has a length of:
e: India's first hyperloop test track, built at IIT Madras with Indian Railways support and completed in December 2024, is 422 metres long and is used to test hyperloop vehicle and vacuum tube technology.

q: In February 2024, the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the redevelopment of how many railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme?
e: On 26 February 2024 the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for redevelopment of 554 railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, along with about 1,500 road overbridges and underbridges.

q: Which of the following Vande Bharat Express routes was among the four services flagged off by the Prime Minister from Varanasi in November 2025?
e: The four Vande Bharat services flagged off from Varanasi on 8 November 2025 were Banaras-Khajuraho, Lucknow-Saharanpur, Firozpur-Delhi and Ernakulam-Bengaluru, so Ernakulam-Bengaluru was among them.

q: 'BRAHMA' (BEML Rail Hub for Manufacturing), the rail coach manufacturing facility of BEML whose foundation stone was laid in August 2025, is being set up in which district of Madhya Pradesh?
e: BRAHMA, the BEML Rail Hub for Manufacturing being built at a cost of about Rs 1,800 crore at Umaria village, is located in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh and will make coaches for Vande Bharat, Amrit Bharat and metro trains.

q: Mumbai's Aqua Line (Metro Line-3), the city's first fully underground metro corridor which became fully operational in October 2025, connects Cuffe Parade with:
e: Mumbai Metro Line-3, the Aqua Line, is the city's first fully underground corridor and runs from Cuffe Parade in south Mumbai to Aarey JVLR, becoming fully operational in October 2025.

q: The Pravasi Bharatiya Express, the special tourist train for the Indian diaspora flagged off in January 2025 under the Pravasi Teerth Darshan Yojana, commenced its inaugural journey from which station?
e: The Pravasi Bharatiya Express, a special tourist train for the Indian diaspora run under the Pravasi Teerth Darshan Yojana, began its inaugural journey in January 2025 from Safdarjung station in New Delhi.

q: The Yellow Line of Bengaluru Metro, inaugurated in August 2025, connects R.V. Road with:
e: The Yellow Line of Namma Metro in Bengaluru, inaugurated in August 2025, runs from R.V. Road to Bommasandra via Silk Board and Electronics City, serving the IT corridor in the south of the city.

q: Indian Railways' first LNG-diesel dual-fuel DEMU train, in which LNG substitutes about 40 per cent of the diesel in the driving power cars, was introduced in regular passenger service by Western Railway at:
e: India's first LNG-diesel dual-fuel DEMU train, in which LNG replaces about 40 per cent of the diesel in its two converted 1,400 HP driving power cars, was introduced by Western Railway at Sabarmati in Ahmedabad.

q: The country's first dedicated maintenance depot for Vande Bharat Sleeper trains, being developed by North Western Railway at a cost of about Rs 360 crore, is located at:
e: The country's first dedicated maintenance depot for Vande Bharat Sleeper trains, costing about Rs 360 crore with a 600-metre track for 24-coach rakes, is being developed by North Western Railway at Bhagat Ki Kothi in Jodhpur.

q: The book 'Think and Grow Rich' (1937), a classic work on personal success and achievement, was written by:
e: Think and Grow Rich (1937), based on Napoleon Hill's study of successful people and his philosophy of achievement, is one of the best-selling personal success books of all time.

q: 'A Promised Land' (2020), the first volume of the presidential memoirs of the former President of the United States, was written by:
e: A Promised Land (2020) is the first volume of the presidential memoirs of Barack Obama, the 44th President of the United States, covering his political rise and early years in the White House.

q: The children's book 'Winnie-the-Pooh' (1926), featuring the bear Pooh and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood, was written by:
e: Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) was written by A. A. Milne, who created Pooh, Piglet, Eeyore and other characters of the Hundred Acre Wood from the toys of his son Christopher Robin.

q: The children's novel 'Matilda', about a gifted young girl with extraordinary powers, was written by:
e: Matilda, about a brilliant young girl with telekinetic powers who outwits her neglectful parents and the tyrannical Miss Trunchbull, was written by Roald Dahl and published in 1988.

q: The children's novel 'The Secret Garden', about an orphaned girl who restores a hidden garden at a Yorkshire estate, was written by:
e: The Secret Garden, about orphaned Mary Lennox who revives a locked garden at Misselthwaite Manor in Yorkshire and transforms herself and her cousin Colin, was written by Frances Hodgson Burnett.

q: The historical novel 'Ivanhoe', set in medieval England in the time of Richard the Lionheart, was written by:
e: Ivanhoe, the historical romance set in 12th-century England in the time of Richard the Lionheart and Prince John, was written by Sir Walter Scott and published in 1819.

q: The allegorical work 'The Pilgrim's Progress', describing the journey of Christian to the Celestial City, was written by:
e: The Pilgrim's Progress, the allegory of Christian's journey from the City of Destruction to the Celestial City, was written by John Bunyan and published in 1678.

q: The ancient Roman epic poem 'The Aeneid', which tells the story of Aeneas and the founding of Rome, was composed by:
e: The Aeneid, the Latin epic narrating how the Trojan hero Aeneas reached Italy and laid the foundations of Rome, was composed by the Roman poet Virgil.

q: The novella 'A Christmas Carol', featuring the miser Ebenezer Scrooge, was written by:
e: A Christmas Carol, the novella in which the miser Ebenezer Scrooge is reformed by the visits of three spirits on Christmas Eve, was written by Charles Dickens and published in 1843.

q: The adventure novel 'Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea', featuring Captain Nemo and the submarine Nautilus, was written by:
e: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea, featuring Captain Nemo and his submarine Nautilus, was written by the French author Jules Verne and is a classic of early science fiction and adventure.

q: The science-fiction novel 'The Invisible Man', about a scientist who renders himself invisible, was written by:
e: The Invisible Man, about the scientist Griffin who discovers how to make himself invisible and descends into violence, was written by H. G. Wells and published in 1897.

q: The adventure novel 'Kidnapped', set in Scotland in the aftermath of the Jacobite rising, was written by:
e: Kidnapped, the adventure novel of David Balfour set in Scotland after the Jacobite rising of 1745, was written by Robert Louis Stevenson.

q: The children's novel 'The Wind in the Willows', featuring Mole, Rat, Badger and Toad, was written by:
e: The Wind in the Willows, the tale of Mole, Rat, Badger and the boastful Toad of Toad Hall, was written by Kenneth Grahame and published in 1908.

q: The celebrated English rendering of the 'Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam', which introduced the Persian quatrains to English readers, was made by:
e: The famous English version of the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, which made the Persian poet's quatrains popular in the English-speaking world, was translated by Edward Fitzgerald and first published in 1859.

q: The Tenth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Tenth Finance Commission, constituted for the period 1995-2000, was chaired by K. C. Pant, former Defence Minister and Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

q: The Eleventh Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Eleventh Finance Commission, which covered the period 2000-2005, was chaired by Prof. A. M. Khusro, economist and former member of the Planning Commission.

q: The Ninth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Ninth Finance Commission, covering 1989-1995 in two reports, was chaired by N. K. P. Salve, senior Congress leader and former Union Minister.

q: The Seventh Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Seventh Finance Commission, constituted for 1979-1984, was chaired by Justice J. M. Shelat, a former judge of the Supreme Court of India.

q: The Hazari Committee (1967), appointed to review the industrial licensing system, was chaired by:
e: The Hazari Committee of 1967, which reviewed the working of the industrial licensing system under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, was chaired by R. K. Hazari.

q: The Talwar Committee (1975), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, is associated with recommendations on:

options.A: The working of the monetary system

e: The Talwar Committee of 1975 was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India on customer service in banks and recommended measures to improve the quality of service to bank customers.

q: The Goiporia Committee (1990) on customer service in banks was chaired by:
e: The committee on customer service in banks appointed in 1990 was chaired by M. N. Goiporia, former Chairman of the State Bank of India, and is known as the Goiporia Committee.

q: The Rajamannar Committee (1969), appointed by the Government of Tamil Nadu to examine Centre-State relations, was chaired by:
e: The Rajamannar Committee of 1969 was set up by the Government of Tamil Nadu under Dr. P. V. Rajamannar, former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, to examine Centre-State relations.

q: The Ribeiro Committee (1998), set up to review the implementation of police reforms, was chaired by:
e: The Ribeiro Committee of 1998, set up on the directions of the Supreme Court to review action taken on police reforms, was chaired by former police chief J. F. Ribeiro.

q: The K. V. Kamath Committee (2020), set up by the Reserve Bank of India, recommended the financial parameters for:
e: The expert committee headed by K. V. Kamath was set up by the RBI in 2020 to recommend financial parameters for the one-time resolution framework for Covid-19-related stressed assets.

q: The Khan Committee (1998), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, is associated with recommendations on:

options.B: Harmonising the role and operations of banks and development financial institutions
options.C: The working of the money market

e: The Khan Committee of 1998, set up by the RBI under S. H. Khan, examined harmonising the role and operations of commercial banks and development financial institutions such as IDBI and ICICI.

q: The Mulla Committee (1980-83) is associated with reforms relating to:
e: The Mulla Committee (1980-83), headed by Justice A. N. Mulla, examined prison administration and recommended comprehensive reforms of jails in India.

q: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO), the United Nations agency for global health founded in 1948, is located at Geneva in Switzerland.

q: The headquarters of UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) is located at:
e: The headquarters of UNICEF, the United Nations Children's Fund created in 1946, is located at New York in the United States.

q: Astana is the capital of:
e: Astana, renamed Nur-Sultan between 2019 and 2022, is the capital of Kazakhstan, the largest country in Central Asia.

q: The national tree of India is the:
e: The national tree of India is the Banyan, chosen for its vast canopy, long life and deep association with Indian villages, culture and folklore.

q: The national bird of India is the:
e: The national bird of India is the Indian Peacock (Indian Peafowl), recognised for its spectacular plumage and cultural significance across the country.

q: Indian Air Force Day is celebrated every year on:
e: Indian Air Force Day is celebrated on 8 October every year, marking the day in 1932 when the Indian Air Force was officially established.

q: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice is located at:
e: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, has its seat at the Peace Palace in The Hague in the Netherlands.

q: The headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations is located at Rome in Italy.

q: World Earth Day is observed every year on:
e: World Earth Day is observed on 22 April every year to raise awareness about environmental protection; it was first celebrated in 1970.

q: Hanoi is the capital of:
e: Hanoi, situated on the Red River, is the capital of Vietnam and its second largest city after Ho Chi Minh City.

q: The 'Yen' is the currency of:
e: The Yen is the official currency of Japan, issued by the Bank of Japan, and is one of the most heavily traded currencies in the world.

q: Tehran is the capital of:
e: Tehran, located at the foot of the Alborz mountains, is the capital and largest city of Iran.

q: The 'Yuan' is the currency of:
e: The Yuan, formally the renminbi, is the official currency of China, issued by the People's Bank of China.

q: World Water Day is observed every year on:
e: World Water Day is observed on 22 March every year to highlight the importance of freshwater and advocate sustainable management of water resources.

q: The Bengaluru Metro, popularly known as Namma Metro, is implemented and operated by the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), which is a joint venture of the Government of India and the:
e: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), which runs Namma Metro, is a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Karnataka with equal equity participation.

q: The Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation Limited (MMRCL), a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Maharashtra, is implementing which metro corridor of Mumbai?
e: Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation Limited (MMRCL), the 50:50 joint venture of the Government of India and Maharashtra, is implementing Metro Line-3, the Colaba-Bandra-SEEPZ Aqua Line corridor.

q: The Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation Limited (GMRC), the joint venture implementing the Ahmedabad and Surat metro rail projects, was earlier known as:

options.A: Metro-Link Express for Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad (MEGA) Company Limited

e: Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation Limited (GMRC), which implements the Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar and Surat metro projects, was earlier incorporated as Metro-Link Express for Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad (MEGA) Company Limited.

q: The Noida Metro Rail Corporation Limited (NMRC), a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Uttar Pradesh, operates the Aqua Line which connects Noida with:
e: The Aqua Line of Noida Metro, operated by Noida Metro Rail Corporation Limited (NMRC), runs from Noida Sector 51 to Depot station in Greater Noida, connecting Noida with Greater Noida.

q: The Madhya Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Limited (MPMRCL), a 50:50 joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh, is implementing the metro rail projects of which two cities?
e: Madhya Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Limited (MPMRCL), a 50:50 joint venture of the Centre and the State, is implementing the metro rail projects of Bhopal and Indore.

q: The Jaipur Metro Rail Corporation Limited (JMRC), which implements the Jaipur Metro Rail project, is a wholly owned company of the:
e: Jaipur Metro Rail Corporation Limited (JMRC) is a wholly owned company of the Government of Rajasthan, created to implement and operate the Jaipur Metro Rail project.

q: The Hyderabad Metro Rail project, described as the world's largest metro rail project in the public-private partnership (PPP) mode, was implemented on the Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) basis by:
e: The Hyderabad Metro Rail project, the world's largest metro project in PPP mode, was executed on DBFOT basis by L and T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Limited, the special purpose vehicle of Larsen and Toubro.

q: In the Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL), the equity of the company is held by the Government of India and the Government of Kerala:
e: In Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL), the Government of India and the Government of Kerala hold equity equally in the ratio of 50:50.

q: Besides the Nagpur Metro, the Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro) is also the implementing agency for the metro rail project of:
e: Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro), besides implementing the Nagpur Metro, is also the implementing agency for the Pune Metro Rail project.

q: Bharat Wagon and Engineering Company Limited (BWEL), a wagon-building public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways with units at Muzaffarpur and Mokama in Bihar, was dissolved in the year:
e: Bharat Wagon and Engineering Company Limited (BWEL), the loss-making Railway PSU with units at Muzaffarpur and Mokama, was dissolved with effect from 5 July 2022 following the Cabinet decision to close it.

q: In the SIDCUL CONCOR Infra Company Limited, which has developed a Multi Modal Logistics Park at Pantnagar in Uttarakhand, the majority equity of 74 per cent is held by:

options.A: State Infrastructure and Industrial Development Corporation of Uttarakhand Limited (SIIDCUL)

e: In SIDCUL CONCOR Infra Company Limited, which developed the Multi Modal Logistics Park at Pantnagar, Container Corporation of India Limited (CONCOR) holds the majority 74 per cent equity, with SIIDCUL holding the remaining 26 per cent.

q: The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL), which is executing the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor, is a joint venture of the Ministry of Railways with the State Governments of:
e: National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) is a joint venture of the Ministry of Railways with the State Governments of Gujarat and Maharashtra, the two States through which the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor passes.

q: The Rapid Metro at Gurugram, counted among the first fully privately developed metro systems in India, was originally promoted by:

options.C: Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services (IL&FS) group

e: The Rapid Metro at Gurugram, among India's first fully privately developed metro systems, was originally promoted by the Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services (IL and FS) group through Rapid MetroRail Gurgaon Limited.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Ghaziabad, which homes WAP class locomotives of premier trains, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Ghaziabad, home to WAP-7 and WAP-5 locomotives hauling premier trains like Rajdhani and Shatabdi services, functions under Northern Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Kanpur functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Kanpur, which maintains WAP-7 and other electric locomotives, functions under the Prayagraj (Allahabad) division of North Central Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Vijayawada functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Vijayawada, a major electric locomotive maintenance base in Andhra Pradesh, functions under the Vijayawada division of South Central Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Royapuram in Chennai functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Royapuram in Chennai, one of the oldest electric loco sheds in the country, functions under the Chennai division of Southern Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Bhilai functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Bhilai in Chhattisgarh, which homes WAG class freight locomotives, functions under the Raipur division of South East Central Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Bondamunda functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Bondamunda in Odisha, a major base for WAG-9 freight locomotives serving the steel and mining belt, functions under the Chakradharpur division of South Eastern Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Angul in Odisha functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Angul in Odisha functions under the Khurda Road division of East Coast Railway.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Itarsi functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Itarsi in Madhya Pradesh, located at the major Itarsi junction, functions under the Bhopal division of West Central Railway.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Krishnarajapuram in Bengaluru functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Krishnarajapuram in Bengaluru, which maintains diesel locomotives for the Bengaluru region, functions under the Bengaluru division of South Western Railway.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Ratlam functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Ratlam in Madhya Pradesh, a large diesel locomotive maintenance base, functions under the Ratlam division of Western Railway.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Siliguri functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Siliguri in West Bengal, serving the gateway to the North-East, functions under the Katihar division of Northeast Frontier Railway.

q: In railway freight operations, consignments which exceed the standard loading gauge dimensions and require special sanction for movement are denoted by the abbreviation 'ODC', which stands for:
e: ODC stands for Over Dimensional Consignment, freight that exceeds the standard loading gauge or moving dimensions and can be moved only with special sanction and precautions.

q: In railway train operations, the caution imposed on the speed of trains for a limited period due to track or other works in progress is denoted by the abbreviation 'TSR', which stands for:
e: TSR stands for Temporary Speed Restriction, a caution on train speed imposed for a limited period, for example during track renewal, maintenance or other works in progress.

q: In railway train operations, the speed limit permanently applicable at a particular location due to curves, gradients or other fixed features is denoted by the abbreviation 'PSR', which stands for:
e: PSR stands for Permanent Speed Restriction, the fixed speed limit permanently applicable at a location because of curves, gradients, points and crossings or other permanent features.

q: In railway train operations, the certificate issued after train examination certifying the adequacy of the braking system of a rake is denoted by the abbreviation 'BPC', which stands for:
e: BPC stands for Brake Power Certificate, issued after examination of a train to certify that its braking system is adequate for the run up to the destination or examination point stated in it.

q: In railway passenger operations, the unauthorised stopping of a train by passengers by pulling the emergency chain is denoted by the abbreviation 'ACP', which stands for:
e: ACP stands for Alarm Chain Pulling, the unauthorised stopping of a train by passengers pulling the alarm chain provided for use only in emergencies.

q: In railway reservation charts, the waiting list code 'TQWL' stands for:
e: TQWL stands for Tatkal Quota Waiting List, the waiting list of passengers booked under the Tatkal quota who could not get confirmed Tatkal accommodation.

q: In railway freight marketing, the long-term arrangement under which freight rates and rebates are assured to a customer against a committed growth in traffic is denoted by the abbreviation 'LTTC', which stands for:
e: LTTC stands for Long Term Tariff Contract, the arrangement under which Indian Railways assured freight rates and rebates to key customers for 3 to 5 years against their commitment of guaranteed and growing freight traffic.

q: In the freight policy of Indian Railways, the private cargo terminals developed under the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal policy are denoted by the abbreviation 'GCT', which stands for:
e: GCT stands for Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal, the private cargo terminals developed on railway or non-railway land under the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal policy to boost rail freight.

q: In container traffic working, a facility where container cargo is stuffed, de-stuffed and custom-cleared away from the port is denoted by the abbreviation 'CFS', which stands for:
e: CFS stands for Container Freight Station, an off-port facility where export and import container cargo is stuffed, de-stuffed, stored and cleared by Customs away from the congested port area.

q: In railway reservation and refund working, the report prepared by the train ticket checking staff recording exceptional cases such as passengers not turning up is denoted by the abbreviation 'EDR', which stands for:
e: EDR stands for Exceptional Data Report, prepared by ticket checking staff to report exceptional cases during charting and on trains, such as passengers not turning up or vacant accommodation.

q: In the railway enquiry services provided on the number 139, the automated voice-based facility denoted by the abbreviation 'IVRS' stands for:
e: IVRS stands for Interactive Voice Response System, the automated telephone facility used on the railway enquiry number 139 to give train running, PNR and other information through voice prompts.

q: The first electric train service in the Kashmir Valley, flagged off in February 2024, was run between Baramulla and:
e: The first electric train service in the Kashmir Valley, flagged off on 20 February 2024, ran between Baramulla and Sangaldan on the newly electrified Baramulla-Srinagar-Banihal-Sangaldan section of the USBRL project.

q: The 'Sanraksha' mobile application, launched across Indian Railways in November 2024 for training and capacity building of frontline safety staff, was first piloted in which division?
e: The Sanraksha mobile application, launched in November 2024 for safety training and capacity building of frontline safety staff, was first piloted in the Nagpur division of South East Central Railway, where it was designed.

q: The first trial train over the Chenab Bridge, the world's highest railway arch bridge, was run in June 2024 on the section between Sangaldan and:
e: The first trial train over the Chenab Bridge, the world's highest railway arch bridge, was run in June 2024 between Sangaldan and Reasi on the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link.

q: Who took over as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Railway Board on 1 September 2024?
e: Satish Kumar, a Railway Mechanical Engineering Service officer and former General Manager of Northern Railway, took over as Chairman and CEO of the Railway Board on 1 September 2024, succeeding Jaya Verma Sinha.

q: The first prototype of the Vande Bharat Sleeper train, unveiled in September 2024, was built at the Bengaluru facility of:
e: The first prototype of the Vande Bharat Sleeper train, unveiled in September 2024, was built by BEML Limited at its Bengaluru rail manufacturing facility.
